text:
maria: Heads-up — after the infra deploy tonight, SAST CI started marking ~2k findings as "owner: unknown". Looks like the scanner can't decrypt stored artifacts anymore. Anyone else seeing this?

oliver: Yep, saw the same alerts. CI logs show a 403 from KMS.decrypt for service-account=scanner-runner@redwood-inference. Did we push an RBAC change to keystore?

scanner-bot: scan-runner: latest job #9842 failed to decrypt artifact /artifacts/sast/9842.tar.gz -> PermissionDenied (KMS)

jake: I made a minimal role change in IAM yesterday (PR #3421) to tidy compute groups — it touched the "infra-deployers" group. Possible we removed scanner-runner indirectly via group membership. @maria can you paste the exact 403 payload?

maria: Pasting error from CI logs:
```
ERROR: 403 PermissionDenied: projects/rdw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/sast-key: decrypt: Permission 'cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt' denied for serviceAccount:scanner-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
job: sast-runner-9842
```

toni: This is an incident for sure — orphaned SAST findings mean we could silently miss critical vulns. @sec-oncall can you stand this up as an incident channel and triage? :exclamation: :thinking_face:

sec-oncall: On it. Creating incident channel #inc-315432-keystore-decrypt. Immediate mitigation: grant temporary kms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on projects/rdw-prod/.../sast-key to scanner-runner, then re-run scans and backfill. I'll also notify product/security owners.

oliver: Quick mitigation CLI (gcloud):
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding sast-key \
  --location=global --keyring=keystore \
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --project=rdw-prod
```

maria: I'll re-run the failing jobs after the grant and kick off a backfill that re-decrypts artifacts and re-runs the SAST pipeline. ETA ~45m. :thumbsup:

jake: Two follow-ups we need immediately: 1) an audit log entry for the RBAC change that caused this (who/what/when), and 2) a premerge test to assert scanner-runner still has decrypt access so future group churn won't break scans.

infra-logs: Searching Cloud Audit Logs... found an IAM policy binding change at ts=3154321800 by user=devops-bot@redwood-inference with delta: removed member serviceAccount:scanner-runner@... via group resolution change. Log entry: projects/rdw-prod/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity/entries/abc123. Retention currently 30d.

sec-oncall: Root cause looks like group membership automation removed scanner-runner indirectly. Action items: 
- emergency RBAC revert and redeploy scanner-runner grant (oliver/maria)
- backfill scans and triage any newly surfaced findings (maria/jake)
- add a presubmit/integration check asserting SAST scanner SA has kms decrypt (jake)
- extend audit log retention for keystore admin events and add an alert on keystore IAM changes (security/infra)
- update oncall runbook to include immediate KMS decrypt checks after infra PRs touch groups (toni)

maria: I'll open a post-incident RFC with the runbook updates and link the PR for the presubmit test. Will also enumerate all service accounts that rely on keystore decrypt and add a guardrail.

toni: Thanks team. Once backfill finishes, let's do a short postmortem in #eng-security and close the incident.

maria: Backfill kicked off — monitoring job logs and will post results in #inc-315432-keystore-decrypt when complete.

scanner-bot: scan-runner: re-run queued (job #9843).

sec-oncall: Closing notes for triage: tag findings detected during gap as "potentially-delayed" until validated; owners should verify severity. Will follow up with the RFC and runbook link. :white_check_mark:
